items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between sessions, so Monday's preference must have been saved outside the window and loaded into Friday's call. Training does not include the chat (a, M3), a big window only holds one session's text (b, M7), and a guess from booking patterns is not what the stem describes (d).

Call 1 is 700. Call 2 is 700 + 50 + 300 = 1,050. Call 3 is 1,050 + 50 + 500 = 1,600. Total 700 + 1,050 + 1,600 = 3,350. An answer of 1,600 counts only the last call, and shows the idea that earlier calls are not paid for again.

An exact code that appears in the manual is what keyword search matches best. Embedding search is good for different wording but is not always better (a), the whole manual re-sent each call is costly (c, M8), and recall from the model's own memory can be wrong or out of date (d).

items.answer: Everything in the window is re-sent and paid for on every later call, so only the few relevant chunks should go in, which also keeps the window uncluttered.
accepted: It saves tokens and cost, since whatever is in the window is sent again on every step.
The whole manual would cost too many tokens on every call and would not fit well; the top chunks are enough to answer.
To keep cost down and the window focused on what is relevant.
items.rationale: Full credit names the cost or window-space reason: tokens in the window are paid for on each call. Saying only that the manual is too big to fit is partial, since a big window could hold it but at a high cost per call (M8).

items.answer: The window is emptied when the session ends, so nothing from this visit is there at the next one unless it was saved and loaded back.
accepted: A window only lasts for one session, so it can't carry information to the next visit.
Nothing is kept after the session ends; notes must be saved outside the window.
items.rationale: A larger window holds more within one request or session, but it starts empty each session, so memory between visits needs saved notes or a database (M7). A cost reason alone is only partial, since the question asks about memory between visits.
